{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZZ7zwg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDBQaQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 25, "title": "Support raw 3 MiB and 6 MiB cartridges with top-aligned ROM mapping", "body": "## Problem

At `63a142f5520c81d317070f5eed8f0962d3393e2f`, `Cartridge::parse` requires power-of-two file lengths while recognizing size codes 05/07 as 3/6 MiB and requiring declared size to equal file length. Consequently, raw images fail immediately; externally padded copies retaining those headers also fail. The diagnostic's leading-padding advice cannot satisfy validation. Simply removing the first check would leave incorrect mapping because `Cartridge::rom` masks addresses by raw length minus one.

This excludes two recognized cartridge sizes before execution on every console model. Removing this barrier improves format coverage; commercial-title playability remains untested.

## Expected outcome

Load valid raw 3 MiB and 6 MiB images without external padding or header changes. Map their populated bytes at the top of rounded 4 MiB/8 MiB ROM address spaces, consistently across CPU reads, startup and DMA. Preserve original image bytes, metadata, checksum validation, reported ROM length and browser save identity.

## Context

Relevant implementation: `crates/ws-core/src/cartridge.rs`, `bus.rs`, `lib.rs`, the thin `ws-web` adapter, `web/src/saves.ts`, fixture tooling and native/browser compatibility suites.

Inspected evidence:

- [Wonderful linker documentation](https://wonderful.asie.pl/wiki/doku.php?id=wswan:guide:memory_management) describes bank placement relative to the top of ROM.
- [Pinned ares loader](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/blob/64c835451157de74e418ca3fdbe1b5aec9972af9/ares/ws/cartridge/cartridge.cpp) rounds backing size and loads image bytes at its upper end.
- [Pinned Beetle loader](https://github.com/libretro/beetle-wswan-libretro/blob/0db0832183ad264bbe67bcd7e651365e7dac5389/libretro.c) likewise rounds/top-aligns data and fills the leading region with FF. These implementations corroborate an addressing policy; they do not establish every physical cartridge's unpopulated-address behavior. Consult behavior without copying emulator code.

Use rounded-address wrapping followed by subtraction of the leading gap: for raw length L, capacity C is the next power of two and populated addresses occupy `[C-L, C)`. Common-interface bank D0 starts raw 3 MiB data; bank A0 starts raw 6 MiB data. The final bank retains the cartridge footer/reset jump. Use FF for the synthetic leading region as an explicit emulation policy, without claiming electrical accuracy.

Assumption correction: the old power-of-two-only restriction and external-padding remedy are insufficient. Separate logical image length from mapped capacity; preserve exact raw header/size/checksum validation. The inspected placement documentation and loaders support this correction. Padded files whose length disagrees with their header may remain rejected with accurate diagnostics.

Current main matches the baseline and the open-Issue collection, including PRs, is empty. Earlier mapper work in #11/#12 and live A0 work in #23/#24 must remain intact. [Saved #23 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/63a142f5520c81d317070f5eed8f0962d3393e2f/docs/issue-23-validation.md) reports 79 core unit tests, nine integration tests and both Chromium suites passing. Those are reported results, not checks rerun during this planning. WSdev ROM-header access failed; accessible alternatives supplied useful evidence.

Scope is image validation and shared ROM mapping with necessary lifecycle, DMA, fixture and browser coverage. Broader mapper classification, RTC, firmware authentication and electrical open bus remain separate gaps.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Accept exact raw lengths 3,145,728/6,291,456 with size codes 05/07. Retain existing bounds, field-specific validation, mapper limits and model restrictions. Test valid images, truncated/extra bytes, declared-size mismatch, unsupported lengths and checksum corruption. Replace misleading padding advice.
- [ ] Implement the rounded/top-aligned map above. Preserve immutable raw bytes, header ROM size/checksum, `load_rom` return length and `rom_len`. Synthetic fill must not enter image checksum or browser SHA-256 identity. Existing power-of-two mapping remains unchanged.
- [ ] Generate original bank-marker images for both sizes and both currently supported mapper interfaces. Assert first/last populated bytes, interior banks, 64 KiB boundaries, rounded-space aliases, leading-region FF policy, C2/C3 and C0 windows, plus relevant 2003 aliases/high bits/self-map reads. Use distinct markers that detect raw-length masking or modulo errors.
- [ ] Native integration tests execute an original reset-entry program for both sizes on Mono, Color and Crystal. Verify last-bank startup, marker reads, raw length, restart and compatible model changes. Failed replacement/incompatible changes preserve running cartridge, live A0 state, cartridge saves and console EEPROM records.
- [ ] On Color/Crystal, verify GDMA and SDMA deliver populated marker bytes through the shared map, including a mapped bank boundary. Preserve live A0 eligibility/costs, DMA counters and existing timing/routing acceptance. Mono gains no Color DMA capability.
- [ ] Extend original source-included CC0 fixtures and the production-preview Chromium/Wasm compatibility suite to load both raw sizes through the existing local file flow on all three models and observe execution/restart success. Check representative common/extended interfaces, exact raw-content save keys, reload/save isolation and separate console persistence. Add no ROM uploads or proprietary software.
- [ ] Coordinator runs and records `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check`; in `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` against production preview. Preserve existing gameplay, audio, A0, DMA, SRAM/EEPROM and browser regressions.
- [ ] Update support documentation, diagnostics, fixture provenance and validation evidence. Record the old assumption, corrected requirement, sources and unverified electrical behavior. Preserve independent implementation ownership, firmware-free startup and thin Wasm boundaries. Coordinator completes source-Issue review and resolves blocking findings before merge. Evidence-based corrections to AI-authored requirements need no human approval or independent AI re-review; preserve the goal and relevant acceptance.

## Optional validation

Compare additional lawfully available hardware measurements or independent software checks. Physical consoles, commercial ROMs and human gameplay are unnecessary for mandatory acceptance. Report optional checks only when performed.

## Required post-merge verification

None

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
